rules.statement: A final decree entered under the Partition Ordinance can be set aside if it was not conducted in conformity with the essential provisions prescribed by the Partition Ordinance, such as effective service of summons on minors who were parties to the action.
rules.supporting_quote: Once the barrier of the sacrosanct character of a final decree is broken through, the reasoning underlying the case of Randeni v. Allis Appu and Fernando v. Fernando (supra) for holding that the decree cannot be set aside fails, and one is free to consider what the effect of minority of defendants is on proceedings in a partition action, where they have not been legally represented.
